newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev softens vs mark, gains vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev softens vs mark, gains vs dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 996-998 per mark on Tuesday, versus 996 at Monday's close due to interest rate-related local mark buying, traders said.
Banks were building up mark positions to profit on higher foreign currency interbank deposit rates. Final clients were also bullish on the mark.
Interbank overnight lev depo rates now stand at 1.50-1.75 percent annually against 3.0 percent on overnight mark deposits.

The lev opened at 1,829-1,831 per dollar, stronger from the 1,840-1,843 at Monday's close, in line with the mark/dollar rise on global markets as local traders adjusted the lev/dollar to the lev/mark and the international mark/dollar crosses.
The lev has been pegged at 1,000 per mark as an anchor currency in an IMF-prescribed currency board system, a fixed exchange rate mechanism introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the lev.
Under the system Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at a fixed bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000.
